html:
On 3 December 1854 soldiers and police stormed a stockade built by rebel gold miners at Eureka, Ballarat, in the colony of Victoria. At least 27 people were killed, most of them miners.

The diggers of the Victorian gold rush were angry at a costly mining licence, harsh police hunts and having no vote. They swore an oath under the blue and white Southern Cross flag.

Juries refused to convict the rebel leaders of treason, and within a year the licence was replaced and miners gained the vote. Peter Lalor, a rebel leader, entered parliament, and Victoria soon adopted the secret ballot. The Eureka flag became a symbol of protest and of unions. See Australia.
